Grubbs Test

Source: R/stats.R
grubbs_test.Rd

Performs Grubbs' test for potential outliers in environmental monitoring data.

Usage

grubbs_test(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
grubbs_test(
  df,
  location_id = "location_id",
  param_name = "param_name",
  sample_date = "sample_date",
  analysis_result = "analysis_result",
  default_unit = "default_unit",
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
grubbs_test(
  df,
  type = 10,
  opposite = FALSE,
  two_sided = FALSE,
  keep_data_object = FALSE
)

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

location_id

Location column name.

param_name

Analyte column name.

sample_date

Sample date column.

analysis_result

Analytical result column name.

default_unit

Reporting unit column name.

type

Grubbs test variant.

opposite

Logical indicating whether the lowest value should be tested rather than the highest value.

two_sided

Logical indicating whether a two-sided test should be performed.

keep_data_object

Logical indicating whether the complete test object should be retained.

Value

A tibble containing one row per outlier evaluation group.

Details

`grubbs_test()` is an S3 generic supporting both `data.frame` and `env_schema` objects.

If the input is grouped using [dplyr::group_by()], Grubbs' tests are performed within the existing groups.

Grubbs' test evaluates whether the most extreme value differs significantly from the remaining observations.

Grubbs' test assumes approximately normally distributed data.

For many environmental datasets, Rosner's test may be more appropriate when larger sample sizes are available.

Groundwater Monitoring

Dixon's and Grubbs' tests are generally most appropriate for relatively small datasets and may be sensitive to distributional assumptions.

For larger groundwater monitoring datasets, `rosner_test()` is often preferred.

env_schema Method

For `env_schema` objects, tests are performed using `.analysis_result` values and respect existing `dplyr::group_by()` groups.

Examples

grubbs_test(gw_data)
